medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Since 1975, the Office of Multicultural Affairs for Health Professions Learners (OMA-HPL) has promoted social impact and belonging, creating experiences that allow learners to thrive. OMA-HPL advises and mentors prospective health professions applicants and current health professions students at the University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health. Under the OMA-HPL umbrella are affinity groups within registered SMPG student organizations. UW SMPH also has a Native American Center for Health Professions, which provides opportunities for growth, professional development, mentorship, research and support. 
OMA-HPL Contact:  
Mr. Manuel Santiago
Director, Office of Multicultural Affairs - Health Professions Learners (OMA-HPL)

medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students requesting a leave of absence work with our Student Services staff. Requests are considered on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Outside of classroom studies, most MD students at the University of Wisconsin become involved in extracurricular activities to relax, make new friends, and follow through on their commitment to help others. Many of our medical students participate in MEDiC, a student-run program that manages seven free clinics serving the underserved in our community. The school also has local chapters of the American Medical Student Association and the State Medical Society of Wisconsin. Other student organizations include affinity groups (e.g. SNMA, LNMA), Women in Medicine, specialty interest groups (e.g. Orthopedics Interest Group, Family Medicine Interest Group), and recreational interest groups. All students are members of a learning community or house. The houses, working with dedicated faculty mentors, encourage formal and informal learning, interaction, and socialization. Each house plans activities according to the interests of its members and the mission of the learning communities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health and the Ebling Health Sciences Library are located in the Health Sciences Learning Center (HSLC) on the west end of the University of Wisconsin-Madison's campus. The HSLC is connected to the University of Wisconsin Hospital and Clinics, the American Family Children's Hospital, the William S. Middleton Memorial Veterans Hospital, the School of Pharmacy, and the School of Nursing. The newly remodeled Learning Center provides instructional technologies, including advanced digital capabilities throughout its lecture halls, classrooms, clinical training and assessment areas, computing facilities, and distance education centers. The building was designed to enhance individual and small-group learning. The facility is close to the Lakeshore Path along the beautiful shores of Lake Mendota, allowing for easy access to walking, jogging, and biking paths.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Housing information is available at www.housing.wisc.edu. Additional private housing is widely available within the city of Madison.  Many of our new and current students find housing information on the UWSMPH Med Student website or through the GroupMe for accepted students to each entering class.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: UWSMPH recognizes gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation as valued dimensions of identity. At the organizational level, UW Health earned the "Leader in LGBTQ Healthcare Equality" designation from the Human Rights Campaign reflecting a decade of progress in LGBTQ healthcare. Specifically for students, we also have a number of programs to foster equity and inclusion in these areas. The Gender and Sexuality Campus Center provides education, outreach, advocacy, and resources for student communities and their allies to improve campus climate and their daily intersectional experiences. The student organization, PRIDE in Healthcare, works to improve health disparities and healthcare for LGBTQ+ people. It also provides a social forum for LGBTQ+ and allied students.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The McBurney Disability Resource Center is UW-Madison’s resource for disability-related student accommodations. We work to ensure all students have equitable access to their educational experience, regardless of their disability status.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
UW SMPH prioritizes student mental and emotional health as well as physical health. Medical students enjoy full usage of the state-of-the-art Bakke Recreation & Wellbeing Center, an approximate 10-minute walk from the health sciences campus. Students also have priority access to mental health providers from UW-Madison University Health Services who are specifically assigned to health professions students. They offer a full range of services including in-person appointment availability directly and discreetly in the medical education building.

To foster community, entering class cohorts are organized into subsets, called “houses.” Each house has a mentor, a current physician with a dedicated, non-grading appointment to advise and mentor students. These mentors play varied roles for students including clinical skills practice, specialty exploration advisor, and residency application and interview coach. 

Consistent with our institutional mission to reduce health disparities, UW SMPH prioritizes recruitment of applicants and matriculants who have experiences and backgrounds in historically underrepresented populations in medicine. To ensure these and all students succeed, our Students Services and Multicultural Affairs Offices hold community-building programs, and work to connect current students with alumni to make sure all of our students know that they belong as UW SMPH students and, more broadly, in medicine. 

Summarized, student wellness is more than regular yoga classes and outdoor walking paths (both of which are available and plentiful). We believe it is a nexus of physical health, mental/emotional support, community-building, and personal identity development. At every juncture and transition from matriculation to graduation, student services staff, faculty mentors, and advisors match corresponding and desired resources to students' specific needs.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: We strive to provide an inclusive, safe, healthy, and enriching environment for learning and working that promotes wellness among our students and employees.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
Travel to clinical sites is a requirement of the SMPH MD curriculum that begins in the first year of the curriculum.  

All students need a valid United States driver’s license and access to transportation to meet this requirement. Exceptions to this policy due to medical necessity will be made on a case-by-case basis by the Student Services Office.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Expected dress will vary as appropriate for the day's educational activities. Activities with patients have higher dress standards.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: All courses provide regular faculty office hours.  Learning Specialists provide academic support including office hours, tutors, practice questions, study strategies, and USMLE preparation.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students interact with patients beginning the first day of school and regularly thereafter. From the spring of second year through graduation, most coursework is patient-based in health care settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction is multi-modal and includes lectures, small-group, independent, simulation, and standardized-patient experiences. There is an emphasis on team-based and inquiry-based learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: A one-on-one longitudinal clinical preceptorship occurs in Phase 1. Four 12-week, integrated clerkships comprise the core clinical experiences of Phase 2. Elective clinical courses comprise Phase 3.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: UW SMPH offers Med*STAR (Study Tools and Academic Readiness), a 3-day comprehensive  program offered immediately prior to the first day of medical school. Participation in this program is voluntary.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Comparative performance in Phase 2 is reported to residency programs via the Medical School Performance Evaluation (MSPE).
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Some learning activities including clinical skills sessions and small group, team-based learning have mandatory attendance. Lectures are variably required throughout the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The ForWard Curriculum at the University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health builds upon our long tradition of educational excellence replacing the traditional model of medical education with one that fully integrates basic, public health and clinical sciences throughout our medical students' education. Key features include team-based learning; hands-on application of knowledge in clinical and community settings; robust inter-professional opportunities; longitudinal skills coaching; enhanced health systems immersion; more flexibility for career exploration; and better intern preparation. ForWard is organized into three Phases across four years:

Phase 1 includes core basic science content integrated with community and clinical experiences. This phase is three semesters, all of year one and fall semester of second year.

Phase 2 includes core clinical training with integrated basic science and public health content. This phase is 12 months, two semesters: spring semester of year two and fall semester of year three.

After completing Phase 2, students break from coursework for dedicated preparation to take USMLE Step 1. This occurs early in the spring semester of the third year, before starting Phase 3 coursework.

Phase 3 includes advanced learning in basic and clinical sciences. This phase is three semesters: spring semester of the third year and all of fourth year. USMLE Step 2 is taken any time in Phase 3, scheduled individually at an optimum time based on each student's schedule and residency plans.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Our school recognizes the great need for primary care physicians and is committed to providing robust primary care experiences and opportunities to help address the community and public health needs of Wisconsin, the nation, and the world. Students exploring primary care will find dedicated programs, clinical experiences and student organizations focused on primary care in Madison and throughout the state. Our Wisconsin Academy of Rural Medicine (WARM) and TRaining In Urban Medicine and Public Health (TRIUMPH) programs train medical students to work with rural and urban underserved patients respectively. While not restricted to students pursuing primary care, the majority of students in these programs pursue primary care specialties.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health has the largest research commitment of any school or college on the UW-Madison campus. Our faculty have active research programs covering virtually every aspect of basic, clinical and public health science, and they educate the next generation of scientists through our graduate training programs. In addition, our investigators are advancing medicine through collaboration with departments and schools across UW-Madison, including engineering, and agriculture and life sciences.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText:
Phase 1: Nine-month academic calendar with a winter (2 weeks) and summer (3 months) break. 
Phases 2 & 3: Twelve-month academic calendar with two, 2-week breaks between the 6-month semesters.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students complete a service learning project during their core clinical clerkships. They may also participate in student-run free clinics and other extracurricular, community service organizations.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: In addition to Phase 3 elective research coursework, students may participate in  research during breaks, through fellowships, or through our Path of Distinction in Research program.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UW Hospital and Clinics, American Family Children's Hospital, William S. Middleton Memorial VA Hospital, and Meriter Hospital in Madison; multiple affiliated hospitals and clinics across Wisconsin.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Student transcripts report "Satisfactory" or "Unsatisfactory" (pass/fail) for all courses.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health is recognized as a statewide, national and international leader in education, research, clinical care, community service and global outreach. As an integrated school of medicine and public health, it provides a unified MD degree program that incorporates the promotion of health for individuals and communities as well as the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of disease for patients in our state, our nation, and the world.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Mission: Together, we are advancing health and health equity through remarkable service to patients and communities, outstanding education, and innovative research.

Vision: Healthy people. Healthy communities.

Values:
* Integrity and Accountability – Every person, every action, every time.
* Compassion – Treat all with kindness, understanding, and empathy.
* Social Impact and Belonging – Advance health and health equity by respecting the rights, dignity, and differences of all.
* Excellence – Strive for the very best in all we do.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants offered admission must acknowledge their offer within 10 business days of receipt. This is in lieu of a tuition deposit.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
LETTER FORMAT
Choose one of the following letter formats: 
1) One committee letter and one individual letter from a non-academic source
2) One letter packet, submitted by your institution with four letters (three faculty, one non-academic) 
3) Four individual letters (three faculty, one non-academic)

MORE INFO
https://www.med.wisc.edu/education/md-program/admissions/letters-of-recommendation/
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Faculty letters may be from science or non-science faculty in any combination. For non-academic letters, choose a supervisor or mentor who will discuss your personal qualities. Letters written by supervisors in research labs can be considered either academic or non-academic. Choose authors who can write a strong letter addressing multiple AAMC Competencies for Entering Medical Students:

Professional Competencies
•	Commitment to Learning and Growth
•	Understanding Others
•      Self Awareness
•	Empathy and Compassion
•	Ethical Responsibility to Self and Others
•	Interpersonal Skills
•	Oral Communication
•	Reliability and Dependability
•	Resilience and Adaptability
•	Service Orientation
•	Teamwork and Collaboration

Thinking and Reasoning Competencies
•	Critical Thinking
•	Quantitative Reasoning
•	Scientific Inquiry
•	Written Communication

Science Competencies
•	Living Systems
•	Human Behavior
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: In addition to candidate assessment, applicants learn about our curriculum, student life, our facilities, research, and what life in Madison, WI is like. The interview day is also an opportunity for applicants to connect with current medical students in informal social opportunities. Please visit this website for further information: https://www.med.wisc.edu/education/md-program/admissions/interview-day/
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: One-on-one faculty/alumni interviews are 30 minutes. Additionally, there is a small-group discussion/interview. Applicants invited for interview will receive additional, detailed agendas about the interview program.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews are virtual (via Zoom). All live sessions are interactive.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Pass/Fail Coursework – We will accept pass/fail (or equivalent) grades for coursework completed during the COVID-19 pandemic or when dictated by undergraduate institutional policies for grading. However, to give us the best sense of your comparative academic preparation, we encourage as much coursework as possible be taken on a graded basis (vs. pass/fail). This is especially true for our prerequisites and all courses that fall under the Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Math (BCPM) category in AMCAS.

Online Coursework and Labs – Online courses taken at accredited institutions are accepted toward our specified course prerequisites and general degree requirements. We would prefer lab courses to be taken in person (rather than virtual) but will accept online courses including online lab courses taken in the spring 2020 term and later.

Medical Exposure/Experiences/Public Service –  We strongly recommend in-person experiences in these areas. You may find it helpful to consult your pre-health advising center if you are still in college or as an alumnus. Additionally, you may want to research opportunities in your local community. Local volunteer organizations may have suggestions for acceptable opportunities as well.

Accepted applicants may select "Plan to Enroll" beginning February 19. Applicants with multiple acceptances should narrow their choices to three schools by April 15. By April 30, applicants should select "Commit to Enroll" for their final choice of medical school, and withdraw acceptances from all other schools. If an accepted applicant is holding acceptances at schools other than UWSMPH after June 1, we reserve the right to rescind our acceptance. Applicants with extraordinary circumstances requiring additional time to make a final decision should contact our office as soon as possible. Applicants may remain on alternate lists at other medical schools after selecting "Commit to Enroll."
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are considered holistically at all phases of applicant selection. They are used to assess both the Thinking and Reasoning and the Science Competencies for Entering Medical Students endorsed by the AAMC.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have a combined score of 500 to receive a secondary application. Applicants with sub-500 MCATs will not be considered.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 to receive a secondary application. Applicants whose undergraduate GPA is below 3.0 but who have earned a 3.0 minimum GPA in at least 12 postbaccalaureate or graduate-level credits in the natural, biological, or public health sciences will be considered.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Applicants with undergraduate GPAs below 3.0 will be considered only if they also completed at least 12 postbaccalaureate or graduate-level credits in the natural, biological, or public health sciences, and earned a 3.0 minimum GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: These courses must be in the natural, biological, or public/population health sciences.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college coursework may be used to satisfy any prerequisite coursework. However, applicants are encouraged to consider the academic rigor of their entire undergraduate course of study - especially the prerequisites - and ensure these provide the best representation of the applicant's ability to succeed in medical school.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: While these documents may be submitted, they will have no bearing on the admissions committee's decisions at any point in the cycle (preliminary review, interview selection, final decision, waitlist). Our process and policies were developed to ensure (to the extent possible) that all applications are reviewed using a consistent set of materials.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health has established technical standards for admission to, continued enrollment in, and graduation from the MD program.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: All financial aid allocated by UWSMPH is awarded on the basis of need. Need is calculated as the necessary expenses incurred while attending medical school minus the resources provided to the student by outside agencies and personal resources.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
We offer a pre-med pathway program called Rural and Urban Scholars in Community Health (RUSCH). It is designed for pre-health undergraduate students interested in practicing medicine in Wisconsin’s rural or urban health shortage areas.  https://www.med.wisc.edu/education/rusch/

We also offer a Health Professions Shadowing Program (HPSP),  an intensive, two-week summer shadowing and professional development program designed to increase access and equity in healthcare for UW-Madison undergraduate students. https://prehealth.wisc.edu/health-professions-shadowing-program/

We also offer the Wisconsin Academy for Rural Medicine (WARM), a special MD program option focused on increasing physicians in rural Wisconsin and improving the health of these communities. Strong WARM applicants demonstrate a commitment to  rural and underserved Wisconsin communities. In order to apply, applicants must hold state residency in WI, IL, IA, MN, or MN. https://www.med.wisc.edu/education/md-program/warm/

Applicants can apply for a combined MD/MPH program before or after matriculation into the MD program. The MPH can be completed prior to the MD program, or during the MD program. The length of the combined MD/MPH program is five years. The MPH program application is wholly separate from the medical school application. It is not a program type available to select in AMCAS. Instead, applicants should note their interest in the combined degree program via the MD/MPH question on the secondary application. The MD and MPH admissions offices will follow up to request the additional application materials for the MPH program.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: Strongly Recommended. You may apply with or without a PREview score. If submitted, scores will be considered holistically throughout the process at all decision points, including preliminary review, interview selection, and final decision.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Acceptances from the waitlist vary each year and are dependent on many factors. Waitlisted applicants are notified of their position and likelihood of an eventual offer in mid-March to early May.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Included in our premedical requirements, an intensive writing course in the social sciences or humanities is required. Applicants should maintain a copy of the course syllabus for verification purposes.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No exact date. Applicants are recommended to review or retake coursework if they feel such a refresh provides a better foundation for medical school.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee seeks exceptional students with diverse experiences and interests. Breadth and depth of academic and nonacademic interests and experiences, ability to communicate with others, motivation for medicine, service to others, personal characteristics, and intellectual ability are some of the factors considered. As a public institution and consistent with our mission and the Wisconsin Idea, UWSMPH focuses on training physicians to serve the health needs of Wisconsin.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: While UWSMPH does not have a minimum (or any) shadowing hour requirement, the Admissions Committee values experiences like shadowing which provide applicants realistic perspectives of the health care field and help confirm their reasons for pursuing medicine. Experiences and activities providing more direct patient contact (e.g. CNA, EMT, medical scribe, translation services) also provide these perspectives and are viewed similarly by the committee.
